prompts.prompt: Exact side view cross-section of Photosystem II standing in the thylakoid membrane. The thylakoid membrane is a deep-teal lipid bilayer running horizontally across the middle; below it the lumen, a pale-gold glowing fluid; above it the stroma, a translucent ivory-cream liquid. Photosystem II is a large glossy green protein complex of two twin lobes spanning the membrane, with antenna proteins around it holding many small glowing green chlorophyll discs; in its middle a special pair of chlorophylls (P680). On its lumen side, cradled in the protein, the water-splitting cluster: four glossy violet manganese atoms and one green calcium atom joined by small red oxygen bridges like a little cube. Two water molecules (one red oxygen with two white hydrogens each) float near the cluster in the pale-gold lumen.
